summary: Handled failures retain original terminal semantics and safe timing; fenced PostgreSQL projection is best-effort and never masks the error.
invariants: Failure recording uses a primitive job ID and copied loaded error payload, never implicit reads of rollback-expired ORM attributes.
The local attempt ledger stores digest-bound, content-free timing; public timing requires a successful fenced PostgreSQL projection.
Timing persistence and projection are best-effort; missing evidence remains missing instead of becoming a fabricated success.
Original error code and explicit retryability survive recording failures; a hard worker or host crash can remain unmeasured.
Missing Chromium metrics, font, QID, visible-text or capacity authority cannot enable provider repair.
Flagged-slide recovery preserves other completed checkpoints; deterministic terminal residuals do not retry the whole deck.
forbidden: Masking the original terminal error with a telemetry failure.
Claiming timing for a hard crash before durable evidence exists.
Provider recovery before exact HTML PNG Chromium preflight authority.
